//: Every setting there is, at its default value. Copy this file, rename it,
//2: change what you want and load it with '!ud play <name>'. Only the lines
//3: that differ from the running game are sent to the other players, so you
//4: can leave the rest alone or delete them - either way they change nothing.
//5: JSON has no comments, so the notes are '//' keys. The mod ignores them.
//waves: How the rounds themselves are built.

waves.//rounds: How many rounds the game lasts.
waves.//budget: Round n is worth budgetStart * budgetGrowth^(n-1). This is THE
waves.//budget2: difficulty dial: the first for a harder start, the second for a
waves.//wait: Seconds of build time between rounds, and a longer breather every
waves.//wait2: so many. Round 1 is not from here - see startTimes below.
waves.//tier: A tier every this many rounds, 0 (scavengers) to 5 (Dragons). The
waves.//tier2: floor rises with the top, which is what stops a late round buying
waves.//tier3: machinegun Vipers. tierSpread is how far below the top a round
waves.//tier4: still reaches: 1 keeps the last generation as chaff, 0 cuts clean.
waves.//composition: How a round's budget splits by weight. Without this the budget
waves.//composition2: chases the cheapest design and round one is 150 scavengers.
waves.//composition3: Weight compares across scavengers, cyborgs and tanks, so this
waves.//composition4: reads the same in round 1 and in round 25.
waves.//special: Odds a round arrives as one weapon family only - a flamer wave, a
waves.//special2: cannon wave - so it can be countered on purpose.
waves.//swarm: Odds of a swarm: the tier below in far greater numbers. No extra
waves.//swarm2: budget needed, since a tier down costs roughly half.
waves.//boss: A boss is a chassis, not a price: cost ranges overlap far too much
waves.//boss2: to say 'Tiger at 15' with a number. The count falls as the game
waves.//boss3: goes on - countStart minus the round over countDecline - because
waves.//boss4: one Viper at round 5 decides nothing and three Dragons at 30 are
waves.//boss5: plenty. untilRound is the last round that chassis is used for.

//budgetVariance: How far a round may drift from its stated budget, as a fraction.
//waveScale: A multiplier on every round, on top of everything above. Apart from
//waveScale2: the waves block on purpose: that is how rounds are built, this is
//waveScale3: what they are worth. Also settable in chat with '!ud scale 1.5'.
//waveSplit: With several Wave Defense slots: false means each sends the whole
//waveSplit2: round, true means they divide it. Either way each slot's own lobby
//difficultyScale: What the lobby difficulties are worth. Same shape the base game
//difficultyScale2: uses for AI power. Each wave slot uses its own.
//startTimes: Seconds before the FIRST wave, by the lobby's base setting. How
//startTimes2: long you need depends on what you were given: starting with
//startTimes3: nothing means a truck, a derrick, a generator and a factory before
//difficultyTimeBonus: Extra seconds on that first round from the wave slots'
//difficultyTimeBonus2: difficulty. A harder setting sends a bigger first wave, so it
//difficultyTimeBonus3: also buys more time to meet it. The hardest slot decides.
//spawnRate: Units released per tick. One at a time let defenders pick a round
//spawnRate2: apart as it appeared rather than face a wave.
//spawnRadius: How wide the Base and Center spawn areas are, in tiles. A wide
//spawnRadius2: area matters as much as a fast rate: units all appearing on the
//spawnRadius3: same few tiles are killed as they arrive however fast they come.
//dropPods: Whether the Drop Pod mode works. Its entry always shows in the lobby
//dropPods2: - Warzone builds that list from files before any script runs - but
//dropPods3: with this off a slot picked as Drop Pod plays as Base instead.
//dropPods4: Distance is how far it must land from every HQ, burst is units per
//dropPods5: tick, warning is how long its beacon shows first.
//vtolsDisabled: VTOL factories locked to zero. This applies to the defenders too,
//vtolsDisabled2: not just the horde - it is a ground game by design. The waves
//vtolsDisabled3: never fly either way: flying designs are filtered out of the
//noBuildRadius: How close to a spawn point a defender may put walls, gates and
//noBuildRadius2: defences, in tiles. Anything built inside is refunded and removed.
//noBuildRadius3: 0 disables it. With Base it is a bubble around the enemy start;
//noBuildRadius4: with Surround it is a ring around the whole edge of the map.
//campRadius: How close a defender's units have to be for a spawn tile to count
//campRadius2: as camped, and how many tiles to try before coming in anyway.
//campRadius3: Nothing is destroyed and nobody is warned: parking an army on the
//hqGraceUntilRound: Until which round a player may be without a Command Center.
//hqGraceUntilRound2: The grace period is what lets you start with nothing and build
//hqGraceUntilRound3: one, or move an existing one. 0 removes it entirely.
//grantHQToAI: Whether an AI that reaches the end of the grace period without one
//grantHQToAI2: is given a Command Center rather than knocked out. It had no way to
//grantHQToAI3: know it was on a clock, unlike a human, who was told in the console.
//eliminateOnHQLoss: Whether an AI defender that loses its Command Center is cleared
//eliminateOnHQLoss2: off the map. Without it the rule only really applies to humans.
//hqBlast: A dying Command Center clears units within this radius - everyone's,
//hqBlast2: so the wave that broke through dies in the blast too. Without that a
//hqBlast3: horde rolls into the next base at full strength and a team falls like
//hqBlast4: dominoes. It travels outwards a tile at a time, hqBlastStep apart.
//hqBlastWeapon: A weapon fired along each ring, purely for the look of it - without
//hqBlastWeapon2: one the blast is only visible where it catches units. It is a real
//hqBlastWeapon3: weapon doing real damage to whatever is still standing nearby, a
//bossCrates: Whether a dead boss leaves a crate holding one of its own
//bossCrates2: components, which becomes buildable for whoever picks it up.
//researchDelay: Seconds to hold the horde's research behind the schedule it would
//researchDelay2: otherwise follow. It gets its upgrades by the clock, not from
//researchDelay3: laboratories, so this decides how far ahead of you its units are.
